data.name: Ganapati
data.gender_notes: Ganapati is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ganesha is the god of wisdom, new beginnings, and the removal of obstacles. He is the lord of the Ganas, the collective group of all other gods, and is also the god of culture, arts, and sciences. The name Ganapati carries the meaning “Lord of Ganas (followers)” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ganapati usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of ganas (followers) and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of wisdom, power, and new beginnings.
data.etymology: Ganapati belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Ganas (followers).”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ganapati total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Ganapati is a widely revered and beloved deity in Indian culture. His image is found all over India, and in various forms like Ganesha Chaturthi, Ganesh Chaturthi festival, popular literature, folktales, sculptures, and more. He is the god to be invoked before starting a new venture or before initiating any significant event, like weddings, housewarming, or starting a business.
data.spiritual_significance: Ganapati is a revered deity in Hinduism and symbolizes wisdom, knowledge, and the essence of new beginnings. He is known as the remover of obstacles and the patron of arts, sciences, and wisdom. According to legend, Lord Shiva created Ganesha to keep Parvati, his consort, company during his absence. Thus, Ganesha is also known as the god of self-deployment, the one who starts tasks, and the one who completes them. By invoking Ganesha's blessings, one asks for guidance, wisdom, and success in removing obstacles and starting new ventures.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ganapati symbolizes the remover of obstacles and the god of wisdom and knowledge. He is revered as the patron of arts and sciences, and invoked before beginning new projects or ventures. His elephant head represents power, wisdom, and the ability to overcome challenges, while his broken tusk symbolizes the shattering of obstacles.

vedic_reference.note: Ganesha, the elephant-headed god, is one of the most popular deities in Hinduism. He is the god of wisdom, new beginnings, and good fortune.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ganesh is the god of wisdom, knowledge, new beginnings, and good fortune. The name Ganapati carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
